clue.text: Fish caught by hillbilly — one at home in the water

definitions.text: one at home in the water

parts.note: the dab is a small flatfish
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a hick is an unsophisticated country dweller, a hillbilly

explanation.surface: A rustic backwoodsman lands a fish, while somebody else is happiest swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the hillbilly beside the catch. The definition describes a small grebe, a diving water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The little grebe is a diving bird that lives on ponds and lakes, truly at home on water.

clue.text: "Go on with melody", nuts implore?

definitions.note: split as imp lore: the body of knowledge about imps and devils

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the quoted words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged crowd begs a singer to keep going with the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two parts of the fodder. The definition must be read as IMP LORE, not as the verb 'beg', which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore about imps, read whimsically, is the study of demons and evil spirits.

clue.text: There's always room in one part of pub or another

definitions.text: There's always room in one part of pub or another

parts.words: There's always room in one part of pub or another
parts.note: a pub's cellar is where the beer is stored, and a German-style beer hall is itself a pub of that name, so the clue's 'room' is both

explanation.surface: A drinker reassures us that some pub will always fit us in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' looks like spare space; it is a literal room, the storage room below a pub, or the Bierkeller kind of pub itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground storeroom for barrels in a pub, and also a style of drinking hall named after one.

clue.text: Husband and mother of Artemis put up here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: in Greek myth Leto bore Artemis and Apollo to Zeus

explanation.surface: A goddess's mother and her husband ask where they might stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' does double service in the surface: lodging guests, and the upward reading of LETO in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where travellers are lodged for the night, the sort of place where one is put up.

clue.text: Officers plunder store for something to wear

parts.note: COs are commanding officers
to sack a town is to plunder it
Boots is a British chain of chemist's shops

explanation.surface: Army officers raid a shop to find themselves some clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTS is the high-street chemist found in most British towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall leather riding footwear of the steppe horsemen, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Outspoken spoken passage

indicators.note: spoken tells us to take the word by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: straight talk is frank and outspoken

explanation.surface: A forthright, vocal man walks down a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: The two near-identical words 'Outspoken spoken' do different jobs: the first is the synonym, the second the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel of sea linking two larger bodies of water is a sea passage.

clue.text: Credulous — but inwardly hard and assertive

indicators.note: inwardly asks for the hard letter to be placed inside the synonym for credulous

parts.note: credulous people are trusting, ready to believe
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A gullible person turns out, underneath, to be tough and pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing forward forcefully and ambitiously, as an assertive person does.

clue.text: Lincoln with his first or second son

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
his first letter, the first of the name Lincoln, is L

explanation.surface: President Lincoln is pictured with either his eldest or his next boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his first' refers back to Lincoln: its initial letter. 'or' turns from the wordplay to the definition, the second child of Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the shepherd killed by Cain was Adam and Eve's second child.

clue.text: Masefield's crafty request, Spooner's cover point

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a shawl is a cover for the shoulders
a tip is a point, as of a pencil

explanation.surface: A poet's cunning plea is paired with a fielding position.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield's poem 'Sea Fever' says 'all I ask is a tall ship'; the request is for a craft, hence 'crafty'. Cover point is a cricket fielding position, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield's poem asks for a large square-rigged sailing vessel, a craft, so the plea is crafty.

clue.text: Names forgotten by stonemason working majestically

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name, so names gives two Ns

explanation.surface: A mason carving stone forgets inscriptions while working grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten by' says the two Ns leave STONEMASON; 'working' rearranges the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction from Italian meaning to be played in a stately, dignified manner.

clue.text: Dystopian author gets nothing right, fortunately

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
things that end well turn out fortunately

explanation.surface: A gloomy novelist emerges unscathed, by sheer luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, the classic novel of a totalitarian future society.

clue.text: Carrot cooked with safest sources of energy?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are heated and stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetable prepared in the most careful way gives one plenty of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of fodder. The surface suggests food as fuel for the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear reactors that run on fast neutrons generate power, so they are sources of energy.

clue.text: Down drink? Whose ale for 21?

definitions.note: 21 is the boxer of 21-down, a fighter in the ring

parts.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
cola is a soft drink
Adam's ale is an old joke name for water, so its owner is Adam's

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whose beer this is, pointing to a packer.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland. Nicola Adams won Olympic boxing gold in 2012; the answer to 21 is BOXER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Adams became the first woman to win an Olympic boxing title, in London 2012.

clue.text: Kippers on these? Mostly wan plonkers

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the synonym is kept

parts.note: pallid means wan, pale
plonker is British slang for a fool, as is ass

explanation.surface: Smoked fish lie on pale fools who seem barely there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kippers' are sleepers, from kip, British slang for a nap, not smoked herrings. Plonker is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw-filled mattresses are what sleepers, people having a kip, lie on.

clue.text: Chapelgoers force detective to probe consecrated bread

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force

indicators.note: to probe means to push inside, so the detective goes into the bread

parts.note: the host is the consecrated communion wafer; hosts in the plural
DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: Worshippers make a police officer investigate communion wafers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' sounds like a verb but is the noun: the Met, London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Wesleyan church worship in chapels rather than parish churches.

clue.text: Singer's knockouts?

definitions.meaning: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer; with 's this is her possessive
outstanding people or things, real stunners

explanation.walkthrough: Lulu, Scottish pop singer since the 1960s; a lulu is also slang for something remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner or something remarkable is a lulu in slang, and the pop star's name with possessive.

clue.text: New Year tends to make us inactive

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Resolutions aside, the new year makes us all rather lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make us' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting a great deal and taking little exercise means leading an inactive life.

clue.text: Bird in pool dropping back — one having wash

indicators.note: dropping back means losing the final letter

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of shared money
I is the Roman numeral for one
a wake is the wash left by a moving ship

explanation.surface: A bird in a pond falls behind, as another one has a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' suggests water but is money, the kitty. 'having' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gull of the open sea, named for its call.

clue.text: Lofty's organised chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lofty has an orderly mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay. Lofty reads like a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious and imposing in style, lofty in manner.

clue.text: Going west, drag empty coach in ravine

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading leftwards, backwards

parts.note: to lug is to drag

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving outside letters

explanation.surface: A coach heads west through a canyon, pulled along empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow, steep-sided rocky valley in North American usage.

clue.text: Spotted animal trapped? Get latest info here

indicators.note: trapped means the animal is caught inside the other word

parts.note: spotted means noticed, seen
the boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A leopard-like beast is caught and the news is posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted animal' looks like a leopard; Spotted is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A board where announcements and news are pinned up.

clue.text: Packer's best friend?

parts.note: a packer puts things in boxes, and a dog breed is man's best friend

explanation.walkthrough: A dog is man's best friend; this breed shares its name with one who packs crates.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog breed suits as a friend, and one who packs crates is a crate-filler.

clue.text: See 8
I say, parking place for poultry

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise, like I say
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Goodness, a car park for chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like a sound signal; it is the exclamation 'coo!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage or pen in which hens are kept.

clue.text: Pipe for pirate with a head for heights

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate of Peter Pan

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pirate's pipe; he has a head for heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links. 'a head for heights' looks like the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriental water pipe in which smoke is drawn through water.

clue.text: Spot marker — it's outside leisure centre after Olympian lord avoids conflict

indicators.note: after says the lord's name comes first

parts.note: Lord Coe, Sebastian Coe, won Olympic gold
X marks the spot

indicators.note: outside means the letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: taken without the apostrophe

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Olympian peer marks a spot at the leisure centre and avoids trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe led London 2012. The middle of 'leisure' (S) goes inside ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To live alongside others peacefully, without war.

clue.text: Poet with the ancient mariner?

parts.note: Alexander Pope was an English poet
ye is the old written form of the

explanation.surface: A poet appears with Coleridge's ancient mariner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ancient mariner' looks like Coleridge's poem; 'the ancient' is YE, as in 'ye olde'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating cartoon sailor man is a mariner.

clue.text: Reactionary Russians — dire 5 with SS?

indicators.note: dire means awful, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 5-across, a sea passage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reactionaries in Russia combine a terrible thing with the SS.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of autocratic rule by the emperor, opposed to reform.
